title: A day in Selçuk
goal: Tell a travel story with all five converbs, and follow a blog post about a day trip to Ephesus.

intro.text: A travel story needs its events in order: *yola çıkmadan önce*, *otogara gelince*, *kahvaltı yaptıktan sonra*, *otobüs gelinceye kadar*. And when you tell it later: *Selçuk'a gideli bir hafta oldu*. Look for all five converbs in a blog post about a day at Ephesus.

exercises.title: Selçuk'ta bir gün
exercises.passage:
Geçen cumartesi arkadaşım Selin'le Selçuk'a gittik. Sabah erkenden, kahvaltı yapmadan yola çıktık. İzmir otogarına gelince Selçuk otobüsüne bindik ve bir saat sonra Selçuk'taydık.

Kahvaltı yaptıktan sonra antik kente yürüyerek gittik. Kapıda bir rehber bulduk. Rehber bize kentin tarihini severek anlattı. Kalıntıların arasında yürürken iki bin yıl önceki hayatı düşündüm. Celsus Kütüphanesi'ni görünce ikimiz de çok şaşırdık: çok büyük ve çok güzeldi. Tiyatronun en üstüne çıkınca bütün kenti gördük.

Artemis Tapınağı'na gidemedik, çünkü oraya ulaşmadan hava karardı. Otobüs gelinceye kadar bir kafede oturup çay içtik. Eve dönünce hemen uyudum.

Selçuk'a gideli bir hafta oldu, ama hâlâ her gün o günü düşünüyorum. Bir gün oraya yeniden gideceğim.

glossary.en: the Library of Celsus, a Roman library in Ephesus

exercises.translation: Last Saturday my friend Selin and I went to Selçuk. We set off early in the morning, without having breakfast. When we got to the Izmir bus station, we took the Selçuk bus, and an hour later we were in Selçuk. After breakfast, we walked to the ancient city. At the gate we found a guide, who told us the history of the city with real pleasure. As I walked among the ruins, I thought about life two thousand years ago. When we saw the Library of Celsus, we were both amazed: it was so big and so beautiful. When we climbed to the top of the theatre, we could see the whole city. We couldn't go to the Temple of Artemis, because it got dark before we reached it. We sat in a café and had tea until the bus came. When I got home, I went straight to sleep. It's been a week since we went to Selçuk, but I still think about that day every day. One day I'll go there again.

questions.q: How did the writer and Selin get to Selçuk?
questions.explain: *İzmir otogarına gelince Selçuk otobüsüne bindik*: once at the bus station, they took the bus.
*Kahvaltı yapmadan yola çıktık*: they left **without** breakfast, then had it in Selçuk: *kahvaltı yaptıktan sonra*.

questions.q: Why didn't they see the Temple of Artemis?
options: It got dark before they reached it
The guide didn't take them there
It was closed for the day

questions.q: How long ago was the trip?
questions.explain: *Selçuk'a gideli bir hafta oldu*: `-(y)AlI` + *oldu*, **it's been a week since**.

exercises.question: Which form fits? *Otobüs ___ kadar bir kafede oturduk.*

why.1: *Gelince* is **when it came**; before *kadar* you need the dative: *gelinceye*.
why.2: *Gelmeden* is **before it came**, and doesn't take *kadar*.
why.3: *Gelerek* is **by coming**: it describes how the subject acts.

exercises.en: When we reached Ephesus, we found a guide.

accept: ınca

reject.why: *Ulaşarak* is **by reaching**. Here it's **when we reached**: `-(y)IncA`, *ulaşınca*.

exercises.explain: *ulaş-ınca*: once they had arrived, they found a guide.

exercises.prompt: After visiting the museum, we ate.
accept: Müzeyi gezdikten sonra yemek yedik.
Müzeyi [gördükten|ziyaret ettikten] sonra yemek yedik.
Biz müzeyi [gezdikten|gördükten|ziyaret ettikten] sonra yemek yedik.
Müzeyi [gezince|görünce|ziyaret edince] yemek yedik.

reject.why: *Sonra* goes with `-DIktAn`: *gezdikten sonra*. (*Gezince* works too, without *sonra*.)

exercises.en: We set off without having breakfast.

exercises.prompt: It got dark before we reached the temple.
accept: Tapınağa ulaşmadan hava karardı.

exercises.prompt: Rehber bize kentin tarihini severek anlattı.
accept: The guide gladly told us the history of the city.
The guide [gladly|happily] told us the history of the town.
The guide happily told us the history of the city.
The guide [gladly|happily] told us the [city's|town's] history.
The guide told us the history of the [city|town] with (great) pleasure.
The guide told us the [city's|town's] history with (great) pleasure.
The guide [gladly|happily] explained the history of the [city|town] to us.

exercises.question: What does Deniz suggest?

context.tr: Yarım saat sonra. Kalkmadan önce bir çay içelim mi?
context.en: In half an hour. Shall we have a tea before it leaves?

options: Having a tea before the bus leaves
Having a tea on the bus
exercises.explain: *kalk-ma-dan önce*: **before it leaves**; *içelim mi?* is a suggestion.

exercises.en: We waited until the bus came.

exercises.prompt: When I got home, I went straight to sleep.
accept: Eve dönünce hemen uyudum.
Eve [gelince|varınca] hemen uyudum.
Ben eve [dönünce|gelince|varınca] hemen uyudum.
Eve [döndükten|geldikten|vardıktan] sonra hemen uyudum.

reject.why: *Dönerken* is **on the way home**. Once you were home: *dönünce*.

exercises.text: Celsus Kütüphanesi'ni ___ ikimiz de çok şaşırdık.
exercises.en: When we saw the Library of Celsus, we were both amazed.
exercises.explain: *gör-ünce*: seeing it set off the surprise. *Görerek* would be **by seeing**, *görmeden* **without seeing**.

accept: It has been a week since I went to Selçuk.
It has been a week since [we|he|she|they|you] went to Selçuk.
It has been one week since [I|we|he|she|they|you] went to Selçuk.
It's been [a|one] week since [I|we|he|she|they|you] went to Selçuk.
[I|We|He|She|They|You] went to Selçuk a week ago.

exercises.gloss: until (someone) comes back (the form used before kadar)
exercises.explain: *dön-* has ö: four-way harmony gives *-ünce*. The dative follows, with the buffer y between the vowels: *dön-ünce-y-e kadar*.
